gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now keeps the existing gpio_wdt lane, the bcm2835_wdt starter tests, and the bcm2835 survey checkpoint reviewable together so the watchdog tranche does not drift across simple-driver anchors.

A dedicated survey gate still matters after the starter lands and master advances because it keeps the validation matrix status plus the remaining bcm2835_wdt gap explicit instead of letting the now-established scaffold imply platform or hardware parity that has not been implemented.

The survey note now records the current master head where the bcm2835_wdt starter, watchdog metadata summary, keepalive-ping and timeout-rearm helpers, probe-time bookkeeping helper, registration summary, platform handoff summary, poweroff-path summary, and remove-time teardown summary are already landed while live platform registration, PM base wiring, and live poweroff-handler coordination remain out of scope.

The bounded starter now covers watchdog metadata, timeout tick encoding, running-bit detection, start and stop register transitions, keepalive ping and timeout rearm helpers, restart intent, halt-partition bookkeeping, a tiny probe summary, a registration-facing handoff or poweroff ownership summary, a platform-registration and PM-base handoff summary, a poweroff-path summary, and a remove-time teardown summary without claiming platform-backed behavior.

The lane now records a tiny watchdog metadata summary for the Linux identity string, watchdog option flags, static timeout bounds, and the bounded start or stop or get_timeleft or restart ops surface so the simple-driver packet exposes the watchdog contract before any live registration path exists.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep watchdog metadata, timeout conversion, keepalive ping and timeout rearm behavior, restart intent, halt-partition bookkeeping, probe-time watchdog-core bookkeeping, registration or poweroff ownership outcomes, platform-handoff prerequisites, poweroff-path sequencing, and remove-time poweroff ownership plus devm-managed teardown outcomes reviewable without pretending hardware-backed execution exists.

A dedicated slice note now documents exactly what the starter, watchdog metadata summary, keepalive-ping and timeout-rearm helpers, probe summary, registration summary, platform handoff summary, poweroff-path summary, and remove-time teardown summary cover and what remains out of scope so the repo does not conflate the starter with full platform or poweroff integration.

The first bounded hardware-validation matrix now names the shared Phase 11 test gate, the watchdog metadata surface, the timeout and keepalive-rearm register-image evidence, the probe and ownership summaries, the landed platform-handoff review surface, the poweroff-path sequencing evidence, the remove-time teardown scope, and the replay commands that keep the bcm2835 evidence packet reviewable without claiming live MMIO or poweroff execution.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary around bootloader-carried running state, heartbeat and nowayout initialization, restart priority, stop-on-reboot setup, watchdog parent linkage, and system-power-controller eligibility before any platform registration or MMIO-backed behavior.

The lane now also records registration-facing handoff and poweroff ownership outcomes so an already-running watchdog, watchdog registration intent, and poweroff claim-vs-conflict behavior remain reviewable before any live PM base wiring or watchdog-core registration.

The lane now lands a tiny platform-registration and PM-base handoff summary that keeps parent attachment, PM-base readiness, register-device intent, and poweroff claim-vs-conflict reviewable before any live platform registration, MMIO, or shared poweroff-handler behavior lands.

The lane now records a tiny poweroff-path summary that keeps the shared system-poweroff callback ownership preconditions, Raspberry Pi halt-partition request bits, and short watchdog restart arming sequence reviewable before any live poweroff callback installation or PM base plumbing.

The lane now records a tiny remove-time teardown summary showing that watchdog teardown stays devm-managed while the explicit remove callback clears the shared poweroff callback only when `pm_power_off` still matches `bcm2835_power_off`, leaving conflicting or unrelated callback ownership untouched before any actual platform remove or poweroff plumbing.

Live platform-driver registration, PM base plumbing, watchdog-core lifecycle wiring, and shared poweroff-handler coordination remain blocked until the lane carries an explicit hardware-validation plan for behavior wider than the current handoff and poweroff summaries.
